clue.text: Penny's splendid spread

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for an old British penny (from Latin denarius)
ripping is old British slang for splendid

explanation.surface: Someone praises a fine buffet laid on by a woman called Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: D stood for the pre-decimal British penny. Dripping is fat from roast meat, spread on bread in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef fat set after roasting is eaten as a spread on toast or bread in British kitchens.

clue.text: Dummy is said to wrinkle

indicators.note: is said tells us the word for dummy is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a nit is a fool or dummy in British slang

explanation.surface: A ventriloquist's doll is rumoured to be getting creased.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit the brows is to draw them together in a frown, wrinkling the forehead.

clue.text: Worry over tons of tableware

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so this piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: to tease is to pester or worry someone

explanation.surface: Someone frets about the huge weight of crockery they own.
explanation.definitionFit: Cups, saucers and a teapot for serving tea make up one set of tableware.

clue.text: A friend keeps place that's cut off

indicators.note: keeps means the word for friend holds another piece inside it

parts.note: mate is British slang for a friend
to put is to place something

explanation.surface: A pal is holding on to a seat or spot that has been severed from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons amputate a limb when they cut it off from the body.

clue.text: Stop here as arranged and disembark

indicators.note: arranged tells us the letters of these words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller tells the driver to pull over here as agreed, then gets out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as arranged' looks like a single phrase, but 'as' is part of the fodder and 'arranged' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting off a boat onto land is the idiomatic meaning of this phrase, the same as leaving a vessel.

clue.text: Folk introducing knight to moral values

indicators.note: introducing one thing to another means putting it inside the other

parts.note: an ethic is a set of moral values
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Ordinary people are shown how a chivalrous knight brings morality with him.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk as an adjective, as in folk music or dress, describes traditional cultural groups, which is what ethnic means.

clue.text: Tory took off correctly from college

parts.note: C stands for Conservative, the party of the Tories
ran means fled or took off
well means properly or correctly

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician hurriedly but rightly left an academic institution.
explanation.walkthrough: CRANWELL is the Royal Air Force college in Lincolnshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The RAF trains its officers at the college in this Lincolnshire village, so the name stands for that college.

clue.text: Social worker in house or shed

indicators.note: in means the worker goes inside the house

parts.note: Leo is one of the twelve houses of the zodiac
an ant is a social insect and a worker in its colony

explanation.surface: A council social worker visits a family at home or in an outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare officer; it is the ant, an insect that lives in colonies. 'house' is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall, its roof resting on the larger building.

clue.text: Transform mum without thanks

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so this word wraps round the other

parts.note: mum as an adjective means silent, or mute
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A child changes their mother but forgets to say thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother; it is the adjective meaning silent, as in 'keep mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to change form, a synonym of transform.

clue.text: Holy man keeps Jerry in place

indicators.note: keeps means the holy man holds the next piece inside

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
a jerry is British slang for a chamber pot, also called a po

explanation.surface: A priest hides a fugitive called Jerry in a safe location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerry' looks like a name (or the cartoon mouse), but it is old British slang for a chamber pot, as is 'po'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a particular place or location, as in a nice spot for a picnic.

clue.text: Drinking, eating pasty and surveying the birds

indicators.note: eating means the drinking word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: supping means drinking in small mouthfuls
pasty as an adjective means pale, or wan

explanation.surface: Someone sips a drink and eats a Cornish pasty while birdwatching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like the pie but is the adjective meaning pale. Swan upping is the yearly count of swans on the River Thames in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual Thames ceremony rounds up and counts the mute swans, which is a survey of those birds.

clue.text: Singer allowed to keep pub

indicators.note: to keep means the word for allowed holds the pub inside it

parts.note: let means allowed
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A vocalist is permitted to retain ownership of the tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a person; it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small finch known for its song, so a songbird can be called a singer.

clue.text: Without resistance English invaders arrive in exclusion zone

indicators.note: without means the named letter is left out of the invaders

parts.note: the Normans invaded England in 1066
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
to land is to arrive

explanation.surface: Invaders of England come ashore unopposed into a forbidden area.
explanation.definitionFit: The strip between two front lines that neither side may enter is an exclusion zone.

clue.text: Manage brief response in leaflet

indicators.note: in means the response goes inside the leaflet

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet or leaflet
ANS is a short form of answer

explanation.surface: Someone handles a short reply printed in a flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to carry it out or manage it.

clue.text: Frolic lands doctor in prison

indicators.note: in means the doctor goes inside the prison

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A carefree romp ends with a doctor locked up in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to skip about playfully, the same as to frolic.

clue.text: Neglect old work

parts.note: a mission is a task or piece of work

explanation.surface: Someone is faulted for ignoring their former job.
explanation.definitionFit: A failure to do something, a leaving out, is a neglect of it.

clue.text: Game in set held by seed

indicators.note: held by means the set goes inside the seed

parts.note: a pea is a seed
a lot is a set or batch, as at auction

explanation.surface: A tennis match where a seeded player holds serve in a set.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is tennis ('set', 'seed'); PELOTA is a Basque ball game played against a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelota is a Basque court game in which a ball is hurled against a wall, so it is a game.

clue.text: Displays sailors' propeller

parts.note: airs means displays, as in airs one's views
a crew is a body of sailors

explanation.surface: A ship's crew show off their propeller.
explanation.definitionFit: An airscrew is the propeller of an aircraft.

clue.text: Bob discovers tool

definitions.meaning: to bob hair is to cut it short, which is what a barber does when he crops a fringe
discovers in its old sense means uncovers, as stripping a sheep's fleece lays the skin bare
a pair of large cutting blades used for hedges or fleeces

explanation.surface: A man named Bob comes upon an implement in his garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is a verb, to cut short, and the setter treats bob, discover (strip bare) and the noun for the cutters as three senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shears are a large two-bladed cutting implement, and as a verb the word means to crop or strip off.

clue.text: Shake a bowl of cereal

indicators.note: a bowl of cereal puts the cereal word before the bowl word in the answer

parts.note: bran is the husk of cereal grain, eaten as a breakfast cereal
a dish is a bowl

explanation.surface: A request to shake up a bowl of breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish a weapon is to wave or shake it threateningly.

clue.text: Wild cheer end of grotto makes resonate

indicators.note: wild tells us the letters of the next word are scrambled
end of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A loud cheer at the back of a cave rings round the walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' turns CHEER into REECH; the last letter of grotto adds O.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-echo is to sound again and again, to resound or resonate.

clue.text: Girl's call about fruit

indicators.note: about means the call goes round the other piece

parts.note: a cry is a call
her is the possessive pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl's voice rings out about some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The cherry is a small stone fruit.

clue.text: Queen tucks into fish and lamb

indicators.note: tucks into means the queen goes inside the fish

parts.note: the chub is a freshwater fish
ER is the cipher of a queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The monarch eats a meal of fish and lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' looks like eating; it means goes inside. 'lamb' is an endearment for a sweet child.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is an angelic child, and lamb is an affectionate word for a sweet, innocent one.

clue.text: Property makes soldier and porter panic

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers
porter is a dark beer, so ale
a state is a panic, as in getting in a state

explanation.surface: A soldier and a hotel porter cause alarm over a house sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like a doorman but is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is land and buildings, that is, property.

clue.text: A horse's cough

definitions.meaning: a horse for ordinary riding or hire
to give a dry, harsh cough

explanation.surface: A horse is coughing.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding horse is called a hack, and a hacking cough is a rough dry one.

clue.text: Mammoth is initially grey in colour

indicators.note: in means the first letter goes inside the colour

parts.note: a hue is a colour

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A woolly mammoth is described as grey at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mammoth' looks like the extinct elephant, but it is the adjective meaning huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth as an adjective means enormous, the same as very big.

clue.text: Religion provides advice in note

indicators.note: in means the advice goes inside the note

parts.note: so (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
a hint is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: A faith offers guidance in a written message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests a letter but is a sol-fa note.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the native religion of Japan.

clue.text: Criminal is more conceited having grabbed money

indicators.note: having grabbed means the conceited word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: smugger means more self-satisfied
L is the abbreviation for pound, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A vain crook becomes even more pleased with himself after seizing cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A smuggler, who brings in goods illegally, is a criminal.
